claims.statement: The image-build subsystem serves two build scopes: a repository scope (a one-repository set built on the repository's default branch, enabled via repo_metadata.image_build_enabled) and an environment scope (an ordered set of up to 10 repositories, enabled via the environment's prebuild_enabled flag). Only image-builds/scope.ts switches on scope kind; everything downstream treats the kind as data.

Image builds are available only when SANDBOX_PROVIDER resolves to modal, vercel, opencomputer, or e2b; daytona has no image support. The provider policy returns null otherwise and the routes answer 501 with a not-supported message.

The image artifact is provider-opaque — a Modal image id, Vercel snapshot id, OpenComputer checkpoint id, or E2B snapshot template id — and code outside the provider adapters treats those ids as opaque strings.

A repositories fingerprint is a SHA-256 over the ordered (owner, name, baseBranch) triples of a scope's repository set, computed control-plane-side only (at build registration and at spawn matching), never by the data plane. Order is significant because repositories are position-ordered and setup hooks run in that order; owner/name are lowercased while branch names stay case-sensitive.

A repo scope always builds the repository's resolved default branch; a session on any other branch computes a different fingerprint and falls back to the base image, reproducing the old base_branch spawn filter.

The sandbox runtime reports per-repository clone provenance (repoOwner/repoName/baseSha triples) and the runtime version in the build-complete callback; the control plane stores them in the image_builds.repository_shas JSON column and runtime_version, which the rebuild cron compares against git ls-remote and spawn selection checks against the runtime compatibility floor.

Image identity is (repositories fingerprint + per-repository SHA provenance + baked runtime version). Editing a scope (changing repositories, their order, or a base branch) changes the fingerprint, automatically retiring the old image until the next rebuild completes.

All build triggers converge on ImageBuildWorkflow.triggerBuild so the per-scope concurrency-1 rule is enforced in one place. The per-scope guard is enforced atomically in D1: registerBuild uses INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS for a building row of the same scope+provider, and a concurrent trigger that loses the race reports the winner's build as already_building; getActiveBuild before registration is only a cheap short-circuit.

Trigger sources are: the scheduled cron (IMAGE_BUILD_SCHEDULER_CRON = "7,37 * * * *", every 30 minutes) which evaluates every prebuild-enabled scope; save-hooks that fire on environment create/update, the repo prebuild toggle, and environment secret changes; and manual trigger routes POST /image-builds/trigger/environment/:id and /image-builds/trigger/repo/:owner/:name.

The planner resolves the repository target and mints callback auth BEFORE the build row is registered, while planBuild — which decrypts secrets and resolves sandbox settings — runs AFTER registration, so a concurrent secret change always sees a row to supersede and the build's now-stale secrets can never reach a still-selectable image.

Build-time secrets are exactly the fold the scope's sessions get: environment scopes fold global + environment secrets (repo-scoped secrets never inherit), repo scopes fold global + that repository's secrets. The build timeout is the scope's resolved buildTimeoutSeconds: global defaults, overridden by the primary repository's settings and the environment's own overrides, capped at MAX_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (3600 s; default 1800 s).

Every supported provider follows the same create-bind-launch lifecycle: the provider creates a dormant sandbox, the adapter calls bindProviderSession so the control plane persists the provider session id (setting provider_session_cleanup_pending), and only then does the runtime launch. A failure after creation leaves the workflow to clean up the created provider session and mark the build failed.

Build sandboxes run the same setup steps a normal session would: clone every repository at its base branch (for environments sequentially in position order) and run each repository's .openinspect/setup.sh in order. In BUILD boot mode a failing setup script fails the whole build and, for environment builds, the error names the repository.

Build sandboxes receive the user-configured execution timeout plus a ten-minute finalization grace (IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_GRACE_MS) so the callback can be delivered and the artifact created. Because Vercel caps sandbox lifetime at 45 minutes, Vercel build execution is capped at 35 minutes (VERCEL_MAX_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_MS - grace); Modal and OpenComputer honor the configured execution timeout up to the shared one-hour limit.

Every build callback authenticates with the single-use bearer token minted at trigger time. Only the token's HMAC hash under the IMAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN_PEPPER pepper (with the frozen domain-separation prefix "repo-image-callback:") is stored on the build row; the store binds every token to the exact provider session id and compares hashes with timingSafeEqual. Token TTL is 2 hours.

The runtime reports build completion to POST /image-builds/build-complete or failure to /image-builds/build-failed with Authorization: Bearer <token>, retrying up to 3 times with exponential backoff. Routes validate the body by schema before auth; a malformed body is a 400 that leaks nothing. Missing/expired/forged tokens map to 401, a missing pepper is 'misconfigured' and fails closed as 500, and rejected completions map to 409.

An accepted callback atomically consumes the token (callback_token_used_at) and persists completion metadata; an exact duplicate is reported as a replay and any conflicting or stale callback is rejected without changing the row. The completion hash binds the accepted callback payload (buildId, providerSessionId, outcome, canonicalized sorted repository SHAs, runtime version, build duration) without placing secrets or tokens on the Queue.

After an accepted success callback the workflow publishes a secret-free Queue command {version: 1, buildId, completionHash} to IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_QUEUE; the ImageBuildFinalizer consumer processes one at-least-once delivery: it drops stale commands by completion-hash comparison, requires the build to still be building with a bound session and consumed token, and serializes provider snapshot/checkpoint work behind a D1 finalization lease (6-minute expiry).

Provider finalization outcomes are classified: only 'definitely_not_created' (e.g., a 429 from Modal or E2B, where the request was rejected before any artifact could exist) is retryable; an 'ambiguous' outcome marks the build failed without ever creating again so a duplicate artifact cannot leak. The snapshot/checkpoint attempt runs under a 5-minute hard deadline.

A successfully created artifact is fenced to the exact build, completion, session, and lease in one conditional D1 update (recordArtifact). If the persistence fence fails, the finalizer re-reads D1 (strongly consistent) before compensating: it deletes the artifact and retries, or — if deletion also fails — quarantines the artifact on the row where maintenance can reap it later.

Mark-ready publishes the ready state: the row transitions building to ready, older ready rows for the same scope+provider become superseded (their provider artifacts are deleted inline by the reaper), and a build that finished after a newer ready row existed is itself marked superseded. Terminal cleanup then terminates the provider session and clears the cleanup obligation only after the provider call succeeds.

A runtime failure persists status='failed' with the error message via the build-failed callback; the failure body is deliberately tolerant of malformed error reports (falling back to 'Unknown error') because a wedged building row must always be movable out of building.

The scheduler tick (cron 7,37 * * * *) performs, in order: republish recoverable finalizations (building rows with consumed tokens and no live lease), mark stale builds failed (building rows older than DEFAULT_STALE_BUILD_MAX_AGE_MS with no callback and no artifact, message 'build timed out (no callback received)'), clean up terminal provider sessions with pending obligations (bounded at 4 concurrent, dispatched per row's recorded provider), reconcile every enabled scope through the rebuild policy, and reap artifacts.

DEFAULT_STALE_BUILD_MAX_AGE_MS is the longest provider-session lifetime plus a 5-minute registration/dispatch grace, with the clock starting at row registration (created_at), not sandbox start; exceeding it just causes a redundant rebuild because the misclassified build's late callback is rejected by the status='building' completion guards.

Each build trigger first runs failStaleScopeBuild — a scoped, best-effort version of the global stale sweep (markScopeStaleBuildFailed) — so a dead building row cannot wedge a scope forever through the concurrency-1 guard; a hygiene failure never fails the trigger.

The rebuild policy, evaluated per enabled scope by the scheduler, skips when any building row exists, otherwise rebuilds for: missing_image (no ready row with the current fingerprint), runtime_incompatible (ready image below MIN_REBUILD_RUNTIME_VERSION), invalid_provenance (missing/unparseable repository_shas or a repository missing from the provenance), and otherwise compares recorded base SHAs against git ls-remote heads (check_branches); branch lookup failures count but never force a rebuild by themselves.

Scheduler-triggered rebuilds reuse the already-resolved target through triggerBuildWithTarget, and the save-hook variant triggerBuildIfStale skips when a ready image already matches the current fingerprint (the cron's trigger check evaluated eagerly); unconditional rebuild reasons (SHA drift, runtime floor) remain the cron's job.

A secret change for an environment supersedes every live image for the scope (building and ready included) synchronously before the response via supersedeImageBuildsForSecretsChange — spawn matching sees repositories through the fingerprint but cannot see secrets, so without write-side invalidation a failed or in-flight rebuild would leave revoked values baked into a still-selectable image. A supersede failure surfaces as a distinct error telling the caller to retry; the rebuild is detached and best-effort.

The reaper reclaims provider artifacts best-effort: failed-with-artifact rows (e.g., a restore-failed spawn leaves a live provider_image_id on a failed row) have their artifact deleted and artifact columns nulled while remaining failed so the error message stays visible; old failed rows are deleted only once artifact-free after 24 hours; superseded rows get their artifact deleted then the row removed. Every provider delete degrades instead of throwing — a failed delete leaves the artifact on its row for the next tick, with cleanup calls bounded at 4 concurrent.

Because cleanup dispatches from each row's recorded provider, switching sandbox_provider requires keeping the previous provider's credentials configured until its terminal build-session cleanup backlog reaches zero; removing them early leaves those rows pending until the provider's own timeout or the credentials are restored.

At spawn, the durable object fetches the latest ready image for the session's scope on the active provider only after resolveScopeEnabled confirms the scope still exists and prebuilds remain enabled — a disabled scope's frozen image never rebuilds, so serving it would drift unboundedly. evaluateImageBuildForSpawn then misses cheapest-first on no_ready_image, missing_artifact, runtime_below_floor (below MIN_COMPATIBLE_RUNTIME_VERSION, failing closed on unparseable versions), or fingerprint_mismatch against the session's OWN repository snapshot.

An environment session matches its environment's image only; a single-repo session matches its repo scope's image (where the one-element fingerprint reproduces the default-branch filter); ad-hoc multi-repository sessions never use prebuilt images. A miss on any condition falls back to the base image — sessions are never blocked on builds.

If the provider restore fails after an image was selected, the spawn marks the image failed via markRestoreFailed (status='ready' to 'failed' with 'restore failed at spawn: ...') so the rebuild cron sees no ready image and rebuilds it, then retries from the base image with a fresh spawn identity; a false positive on an unrelated create failure costs only one rebuild.

Sessions booted from a prebuilt image run in REPO_IMAGE or SNAPSHOT_RESTORE boot mode (from the FROM_REPO_IMAGE / RESTORED_FROM_SNAPSHOT env flags), where setup scripts are not re-run — the main source of time savings — and a fast git sync pulls commits pushed since the image was built.

The image_builds D1 table is the registry and state machine: statuses building → ready/failed/superseded; supersede scope is (scope_kind, scope_id, provider) with the fingerprint covering branches, so at most one live image per scope+provider. Public-status reads project exactly the wire columns; internal columns (callback token hash, provider session/image ids, finalization lease, completion hash) never reach a client.

The ImageBuildProviderDeps type pairs the configured provider with its planner — the pair is either supplied together or the workflow is unconfigured, making the invalid provider-without-planner state unconstructible; createImageBuildWorkflowFromEnv resolves the provider from SANDBOX_PROVIDER, throws workflow-unavailable when no provider or WORKER_URL is configured, and validates provider configuration before any database work so a bad deployment cannot accumulate failed rows.

Modal image-build sessions use a dormant sandbox created by the control plane; the runtime waits for the callback token over stdin (the --await-modal-image-build-token-stdin-v1 protocol) after provider binding, then runs the build. Modal snapshot deletion is a local no-op pending the experimental image_delete API, so reaped Modal images are retained provider-side.

OpenComputer checkpoint finalization retains the build sandbox's secret store (deleteSecretStore: false) because an OpenComputer checkpoint keeps its build sandbox's secret store as a base layer that every from-checkpoint fork re-merges; deleting it made spawns fail with 'secret store not found'. Failed builds, which produced no checkpoint, delete the store with the sandbox.

E2B image builds pause the build sandbox with memory disabled, reconnect cold, scrub the supervisor log (which may inherit build-time secrets printed by setup hooks) using a fresh envd token, and create a standalone snapshot template; the snapshot does not reference the build sandbox, so the box can be killed once the build is done (E2B stop only pauses, so the adapter deletes rather than stops).

The web session-target picker annotates prebuild-enabled repositories and environments with 'prebuilt', 'prebuild building', 'prebuild failed', or 'prebuilds on' (enabled, no completed build for the current fingerprint); disabled scopes are unannotated. A repository's annotation reflects its default-branch prebuild state and does not react to the picker's branch selector.

The web app mirrors the control plane's provider union in REPO_IMAGE_PROVIDERS (modal, vercel, opencomputer, e2b) and derives the identical 501 message, so a provider gains image-build support in both places or neither.

The sandbox runtime manifest defines minimumCompatibleGeneration and minimumRebuildGeneration (both currently 60), which become the spawn floor (MIN_COMPATIBLE_RUNTIME_VERSION) and the rebuild floor (MIN_REBUILD_RUNTIME_VERSION); these are bumped only on breaking runtime changes, never on routine CACHE_BUSTER bumps, and v60 is the first generation whose managed-provider plugins use the generic token broker.
